title: SPEC B review and rewrite: cost, decomposition, stacked PRs

completion_criteria.text: The .claude directory organisation is audited and a target layout decided, with the rename's blast radius enumerated and its execution scoped to a branch outside this thread.
SPEC B is reviewed line by line against the repository and its wrong or unreproducible citations are corrected, starting with the *_SCHEMA count and the figures no committed script reproduces.
The questions SPEC B leaves open are brainstormed to a decision, above all the instrument source in section 2.2 that section 8 names the single largest open question.
The two open research passes complete, and a cited report carrying the corrected architecture, the tree and sequence diagrams, and the gap analysis is produced and REVIEWED by the user.
The revised SPEC B is written and approved by the user, superseding the 2026-08-06 document, with every changed claim carrying a citation re-derived at the time of writing.
A successor thread is opened for SPEC B implementation, and this thread closes with no implementation work started.

spine.active_goal: Keep understanding and modifying the architecture page until the user is satisfied with it, then write the SPEC that supersedes SPEC B.
spine.next_step: Start the cache-expiry probe FIRST because it is clock-bound, not effort-bound: create a session, wait past the one-hour cache window, resume, read the cost. While it waits, measure the orchestrator's real context curve to settle the hold-less question - if fill never approaches the limit, rotation is moot. Only if it does, design-pass resumeSessionAt against 0342's four tiers, which needs forkSession and resumeSessionAt measured together. c1's figure re-derivation is delegable in parallel.
spine.last_session: Probed the Agent SDK session/resume contract by RUNNING it (SDK 0.3.228, claude 2.1.228, ~$0.42, 10/10). Overturned 0325's cost clause, split 0342, found host auto-compaction ON at 167,000. Recorded 0348-0350; artifact and probe harness preserved outside the scratchpad. No SPEC text.

open_risks.text: Engineer the escalation step into the phase contract rather than instructing the orchestrator to raise concerns — agents guess instead of stopping in 55.8-67.8% of runs and refuse in at most 2.5%, so a prompt asking for escalation is not a control

Copy decisions, constraints and failures VERBATIM into the rotation brief, never through a summarizer — passing them through one drops constraints across a 0-59% range over seven models with a 30% pooled average, while verbatim pinning restores 0% at roughly 47 tokens

Treat the mid-flight rotation story as designed but unproven — the in-flight registry and idempotency keys on run id plus step id are what stop an orphaned child or a second pull request for a step that already completed
Expect a newly named MCP tool to escape the deny list — the repository's origin-agnostic bash-text gate cannot back that list up, because an SDK MCP call carries no shell text to match against

Reject bypassPermissions at supervisor startup rather than discouraging it — it propagates to every subagent, cannot be overridden per agent, and erases every enforcement layer below hooks and deny rules

Deny the shell and the agent-spawn tool by BARE NAME and never by scoped pattern — a bare name removes the tool from the model's visible list, while a scoped pattern leaves it visible and filters only the argument shapes someone thought of
Pin the subagent spawn depth explicitly if the topology is meant to be flat — the default permits workers to spawn their own workers
Read run-engine.mjs facts as describing a fork the engine never executes — mitosis.js defines its own runEngine that has diverged about 77 lines from it
Never claim mitosis asks a human today — the escalate verb parks the unit and surfaces only in the report a human reads after the run returns

Measure the orchestrator's real context curve before committing to rotation — the fill sensor now exists and works, so whether a routing orchestrator ever approaches the limit is measurable rather than arguable, and a low curve makes the rotation mechanism unnecessary

Price a resume AFTER the prompt cache expires before any cost figure enters the SPEC — the cheap rehydration that was measured ran inside the one-hour cache window, and the full-rate case is the number cost planning actually needs
Run forkSession together with resumeSessionAt before the rotation design pass concludes — branching a rotation is the one combination never measured, and 0349's evaluation depends on it
Re-supply the orchestrator's system prompt on every resume — it is not saved with the session, so a resumed orchestrator silently loses its instructions unless the host passes them again
Run the orchestrator in streaming-input mode — the context-fill sensor is unreachable in single-shot mode, where it throws instead of returning a reading
Re-derive the 167,000 auto-compaction threshold for the model the orchestrator actually runs — it and the 200,000 window were measured on Haiku 4.5 only

Render the rewritten page in a real browser before trusting any of it — two new mermaid diagrams were added and never displayed, and a syntax error fails silently to an empty box rather than to an error

Rename the escalate verb or redefine its mapping in the SPEC — the existing supervisor maps escalate to status parked, so if the new host inherits that vocabulary every fallthrough escalation shelves the MSP instead of reaching a human

Pick a launcher filename other than supervisor.mjs before any file is written — that name belongs to the mitosis fault-recovery supervisor itself, so the collision would be inside the same system rather than with a stranger, which is worse than previously recorded

Re-derive every unverified figure before the SPEC cites it — the phase-literal count came back 48 from one audit and 50 from another, the prompt-byte figures were never re-derived, and the mitosis.js line citations were carried forward unconfirmed

Re-adopt the eight-phase model explicitly in the SPEC rather than citing the 2026-07-30 document — SPEC B's preamble disclaims all citation authority from that document, so a citation to it carries nothing
Read the phase design with git show on branch docs/mitosis-core-rebuild-spec — it was never merged to main, so a working-tree search misses it and wrongly concludes no phase model exists

Make Tier 2 record emission structural rather than voluntary — the design still asks the orchestrator to CHOOSE to emit a typed record, which is the same class of soft judgment as the summarizer it replaces
Keep implementation out of this thread entirely — its criteria are research, artifact and writing only, and a successor thread owns every code change the SPEC calls for
Do not switch branches in the primary checkout — live config entries resolve into the release rather than the working tree, so read other branches with git show instead

key_decisions.title: SPEC B is reviewed and rewritten in its own thread before any implementation thread opens
Orchestration leaves the Workflow sandbox for an Agent SDK supervisor process
Zero variance means instructions are binding, not that model output is reproducible
A new SPEC supersedes SPEC B rather than amending it in place
The architecture report is produced and reviewed before the superseding SPEC is written
The rotation trigger is an absolute token count, calibrated before it is fixed
The orchestrator judges inside phases and never reorders, skips or re-runs them
The architecture artifact is a visual-explainer diagram page, not a report-skill deliverable
The rotation threshold is 200K absolute tokens, and the counting field is the open question
Rotation fires at 200,000 tokens of true context occupancy, not input_tokens alone
Orchestrator autonomy is gated on evidence class, and 0330 is amended to permit typed cross-phase re-entry
The eight-phase collapse is re-adopted, re-derived against today's engine, with four amendments
The stale superpowers-parallel tree is renamed to lib/mitosis as a pure move before the SPEC
Logbook's progressive-summary spine is rejected as the rotation summarizer
Cross-rotation state is tiered by who can be trusted to author it, not by size
No mechanism may drop content without leaving a marker that content was dropped
0325's accepted cost is retracted: the SDK host keeps native resume, fork, rewind and a fill sensor
Plain resume is not a rotation, but resumeSessionAt is a measured fill-reducing primitive
The supervisor disables host auto-compaction and owns rotation below the 167,000-token threshold

out_of_scope: Implementing any part of SPEC B, which a successor thread owns
Editing SPEC A or the config staging and promotion machinery it shipped
The fix pipeline, excluded by the user from both SPECs
